acceptance.evidence: test/index.test.js "AC-1: seeds Work and Home, dedupes names, rejects an empty one, and tags the seeded items" checks the exact category rows, the UNIQUE and CHECK rejections, that category_id is nullable, the items_category_id index and the seeded tags. Implemented in migrations/0003_item_categories.sql.

test/index.test.js "AC-2: an insert naming only title still works; an unknown category_id is rejected" checks that a title-only insert gives a null category_id and that category_id 999 is rejected with FOREIGN KEY.

test/index.test.js "AC-3: / lists every item in id order..." checks status 200, the title order including an uncategorised item, the exact <li> markup with the span, and the plain <li> for an item with no category.

test/index.test.js "AC-4: / shows All first..." adds a lower-case empty category 'errands' that only sorts correctly case-insensitively. It checks the link order and hrefs, and that only All carries aria-current.

test/index.test.js has two AC-5 tests. One checks that only Work's items show, in id order, with only Work current (an unfiled item is excluded). The other checks that ?category=Work&x=1 and ?x=1 give byte-identical pages.
test/index.test.js "AC-6: a category with no items says so, with the filter links" checks 200, the message, no <li>, and the filter links with Garden current.

test/index.test.js "AC-7: a name that needs encoding and escaping..." checks the escaped span and link label, that no raw <x> appears, the href /?category=R%26D%20%3Cx%3E, and that following the link lists only Prototype.

The test/index.test.js it.each "AC-8: %s is a broken link" covers all five URLs. It checks 404, the message, the exact Go back anchor with href "/", that the referrer/origin/history.back script is present, and that there is no <li> or <nav>.
test/index.test.js "AC-9: HEAD answers like GET" checks HEAD statuses 200, 200 and 404 for /, /?category=Work and /?category=Wrok.

The spec marks AC-10 verified by review with a browser step. I could not run a browser in this environment, so I did not verify it myself. The step also says to 'navigate to /?category=Wrok' from /?category=Home. The app has no link to that URL, and typing it sends no referrer. Followed that way, the step lands on / rather than /?category=Home, so the expected result can't be reproduced as written. No test exercises the script's behaviour; the AC-8 test only checks that the source text is present.

traffic/routes.json lists /?category=Work. tests/traffic-config.test.sh has the 'AC-11: a route with a query string passes' case plus bad cases for whitespace, '#' and a route without a leading slash. test/traffic.test.js has two AC-11 tests, one that the route is listed and one that the fake app sees path+query. test/index.test.js "AC-11: the filter route listed for synthetic traffic answers 2xx" covers the 2xx answer.

Existing tests in test/index.test.js cover the behaviour: healthz, 404 /nope, 405 POST,

Items

, escaping, 'No items yet.' and the updated First item markup. But no test names AC-12 in its title or body, and the spec does not mark AC-12 verified by review. Under the review rules an item no test names is unmet.

test/apply-migrations.js drops tables in one batch with PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = ON. test/index.test.js "AC-13: the test reset copes with the foreign key..." inserts a categorised row and expects exactly 4 items, which fails if a previous test's rows survived. A failed drop would break every test's beforeEach. I could not run the suite here (vitest is not installed).

findings.what: AC-10 is 'verified by review', but the step can't produce its stated result as written. The app has no link to /?category=Wrok, so the reviewer has to type it. A typed URL sends no referrer, so 'Go back' goes to / and not to /?category=Home. No automated check covers the script's behaviour either; AC-8 only matches its source text. I could not verify the item.
findings.fix: Make the step followable, for example: open /?category=Home, then run location.href='/?category=Wrok' in the console (this sets a same-origin referrer), click Go back and land on /?category=Home. Then have the reviewer actually perform it, or add a slow-tier browser test.

findings.what: No test names AC-12, and the spec doesn't mark it verified by review, so the item has no named evidence. The regression tests exist: renders the seeded items, escapes HTML, says so when the table is empty, healthz, 404s, 405s.
findings.fix: Tag the existing regression tests that prove AC-12 with 'AC-12' in their titles.

findings.what: States table row '`/`, no items' requires 200, filter links shown with All current, and 'No items yet.'. The only test for that state ('says so when the table is empty') checks the message alone. A regression that dropped the filter links or the status on an empty table would pass. The 'Go back' hidden column of rows 1–4 is never asserted either.
findings.fix: In the empty-table test, also assert status 200, that currentLinks(html) equals ['All'], and that there is no 'Go back' link. For the known-category rows, assert that 'Go back' is absent.

findings.what: The spec records a new coupling: a migration that renames or removes the Work category must update traffic/routes.json in the same change, or synthetic traffic fails in production. Only the spec mentions this. CLAUDE.md's conventions, README.md and the migration's comment don't, so a future agent changing categories would break production checks.
findings.fix: Add a line to CLAUDE.md's synthetic-traffic convention (and/or a comment in migrations/0003_item_categories.sql) saying that routes in traffic/routes.json may name data, such as /?category=Work, and must be updated when that data is renamed or removed.

findings.what: The Go back script requires `ours && history.length > 1`. The decision says it goes back exactly when document.referrer is same-origin, and it names history.length > 1 as a rejected approach. The extra guard is harmless (it avoids a no-op back in a new tab), but it departs from the decision as written without the spec recording it.
findings.fix: Either drop the history.length check, or record in the spec's decisions that it is kept as an extra guard for same-origin links opened in a new tab.

lenses.note: The spec's Go is recorded (commit c72b0f1) before any implementation commit. No implementation commit edits the spec.

Every decision is implemented: schema, seed, URLSearchParams exact match, NOCASE link order, markup, the 404 page, HEAD, routes.json and the test reset. AC-10's review step can't be followed as written, and AC-12 is not named by any test.

I could not run `npm test` here (vitest: not found, dependencies not installed). CI runs it via scripts/check-fast.sh, along with tests/run.sh, which includes traffic-config.test.sh. The tests read as behavioural and would fail on broken code. The gaps are the empty-table state row and the missing AC-12 naming.
README.md is updated for the filter and the 404. The routes.json/category-name coupling is not documented outside the spec.
src/index.js, scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs, test/apply-migrations.js and migrations/0003 were reviewed. Queries are parameterised and names are escaped in the label, span and href.
Category names are HTML-escaped and URL-encoded, SQL is bound, and the inline script uses no input. No planted instructions found in the repo content.

The diff changes server-rendered HTML in src/index.js (filter nav, category span, 404 page). Markup follows the spec's decisions. The broken-link page adds an

Broken link

, which the spec neither asks for nor forbids.
The UI flow in src/index.js was traced by reading the code. No browser was available, so AC-10's Go back was not exercised.
